data.narrative:
Avalanche Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Robin Langtry and Brian Riordan that has raised $80M to date. The sector comp universe includes nine private firms and one public company (Lanzatech, LNZA), though no direct peer set exists at sufficient scale—zero same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy screening criteria.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $80M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $160M. This method is grounded in typical Series A advancement patterns where capital efficiency and de-risking support doubling on progression to the next funding stage. Peer-median comparison was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient comparable datapoints; the broader sector peer set (Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen) lacks homogeneity in stage and valuation tier necessary for reliable triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $136M–$184M with a median of $160M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity bounds around the stage-progression output, the sole applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-stage peer validation and reliance on capital raised as a valuation proxy—an approach appropriate at Series A but subject to variance based on deployment burn rate, technical progress milestones, and sector-specific capital efficiency trends not available in the provided dataset.
